1.title: Maintain and Monitor Pipelines
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Maintain and Monitor Pipelines. This module covers the task statement: maintain and monitor data pipelines. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Deploy logging and monitoring so pipelines are auditable and traceable. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics, alarms and notifications to send alerts. Troubleshoot performance and maintain A W S Glue and Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce) pipelines. Use A W S CloudTrail to track A P I calls. Use CloudWatch Logs to log application data, with a focus on configuration and automation. Analyze logs with Athena, E M R, OpenSearch Service and CloudWatch Logs Insights.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Watches the Pipeline
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Watches the Pipeline. The pipeline finished two hours late last Tuesday and nobody knew until a customer called. Glue job runtime doubled after a source change. A new engineer deleted a table: who did it? Your job: see problems early, alert the right people, and find the cause fast.

1.title: What to Monitor and Why
1.text: What to Monitor and Why. Metrics (numbers over time). Tool: Amazon CloudWatch. Answers: Is it healthy and fast? (runtime, errors, lag, throughput, capacity). Logs (event text). Tool: CloudWatch Logs. Answers: What happened in this run? A P I activity. Tool: A W S CloudTrail. Answers: Who did what, when, from where (changes and access)? Events. Tool: Amazon EventBridge. Answers: State changes (job failed, crawler finished) to react. Alerts. Tool: CloudWatch alarms to Amazon S N S (Simple Notification Service). Answers: Tell people or systems. Exam tip: Metrics, logs and CloudTrail answer different questions: performance (CloudWatch metrics), what the code said (CloudWatch Logs), who changed something (CloudTrail).

1.title: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications
1.text: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications. The figure shows this: The monitoring loop: services emit metrics and logs, metric filters turn log patterns into metrics, alarms watch thresholds, and S N S notifies people or starts automation. Metrics: services publish them automatically (Glue job metrics, Kinesis IteratorAgeMilliseconds and throughput, Lambda errors and throttles and duration, Step Functions failed executions, DynamoDB throttled requests, Redshift C P U and queue length, E M R cluster and Yarn (Yet Another Resource Negotiator) metrics, M W A A (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) scheduler and worker health); you can publish custom metrics (record counts, data freshness) with the S D K (software development kit) or the embedded metric format.

1.title: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications, continued. Alarm: watches one metric (or a math expression) and is in O K, alarm or insufficient data; set the threshold, period and number of data points; composite alarms combine alarms to reduce noise; anomaly detection learns a normal band. Alarm actions: notify an S N S topic (email, S M S (Short Message Service), chat, ticket, Lambda), start an automatic fix (Lambda, Systems Manager, Auto Scaling), or stop or recover an E C two (Elastic Compute Cloud) instance. Dashboards show metrics together; Managed Grafana is the alternative. EventBridge rules catch state-change events (Glue job failed or timeout, crawler failed, E M R step failed) and route them to S N S or Lambda.

1.title: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Notifications, continued. Useful pipeline alarms: job failed or ran longer than normal, stream iterator age rising (consumers lagging), Lambda errors or throttles, D L Q (dead-letter queue) depth above zero, data freshness (no new data in N hours), zero rows written. Delay notification threshold on a Glue job warns when a run takes longer than expected. Exam tip: "Alert the team when a Glue job fails" to EventBridge rule on the Glue job state change (or a CloudWatch alarm) to an S N S topic. "Know that Kinesis consumers are falling behind" to alarm on GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds.

1.title: CloudWatch Logs
1.text: CloudWatch Logs. CloudWatch Logs stores log events in log groups (an application or job) and log streams (a source, such as one run); services send logs there: Lambda, Glue (including continuous logging so logs appear during the run), E C S (Elastic Container Service) (the awslogs driver), A P I Gateway, M W A A, Step Functions (Express), E C two (via the CloudWatch agent).

1.title: CloudWatch Logs, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Logs, continued. Configuration and automation focus:; Set retention per log group (the default is never expire) to control cost; Create log groups and permissions with infrastructure as code; Metric filters turn patterns in logs into metrics (count error lines), which feed alarms; Subscription filters stream log events in near real time to Kinesis Data Streams, Data Firehose or Lambda (and from there to S three or OpenSearch); cross-account delivery is supported; Export to S three for archives and Athena; Use structured Jason logs with run I D, step and record counts, and log levels; Log classes (Standard and Infrequent Access) trade features for lower cost.

1.title: CloudWatch Logs, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Logs, continued. CloudWatch Logs Insights: a query language to search and analyze log groups interactively: fields, filter, stats, sort, limit, parse.

1.title: CloudWatch Logs, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Logs, continued. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: CloudWatch Logs, continued
1.text: CloudWatch Logs, continued. CloudWatch Logs Insights. Quick interactive queries on recent logs in CloudWatch. Amazon Athena. S Q L over logs in S three (CloudTrail, E L B (Elastic Load Balancing), V P C (Virtual Private Cloud) flow, application logs) at low cost; use partitioning or partition projection. Amazon OpenSearch Service. Search, dashboards and real-time log analytics (ingest through Firehose or subscription filters). Amazon E M R (Spark). Very large volumes and custom processing of big data application logs. Glue or Spark. Batch parsing and enrichment of raw logs into Parquet. Exam tip: "Run S Q L on years of logs in S three cheaply" to Athena (partitioned). "Near-real-time search and dashboards over logs" to OpenSearch Service fed by Firehose. "Count error lines and alarm" to metric filter plus alarm.

1.title: AWS Glue
1.text: A W S Glue. Turn on: job metrics, observability metrics, continuous logging and the Spark U I (event logs in S three). Read: CloudWatch driver and executor memory, executors running, bytes read and written; job run insights for root causes; the Spark U I for skew, shuffle and stage time. Typical fixes: bigger or memory-optimized workers, more workers (or auto scaling), fix skew, group small files, push down filters, enable bookmarks, raise timeouts only for a reason.

1.title: AWS Glue, continued
1.text: A W S Glue, continued. Maintain: update scripts and libraries, move to current Glue versions, rotate secrets, review failed runs, keep job parameters in code, and review the pipeline against the Well-Architected pillars with the A W S Well-Architected Tool.

2.title: Amazon EMR
2.text: Amazon E M R. Logs: step logs, container logs (Yarn) and node logs; E M R archives logs to S three at a set interval (turn on log U R I (Uniform Resource Identifier) so logs survive cluster termination). Monitor: CloudWatch metrics (applications running, Yarn memory available, H D F S (Hadoop Distributed File System) utilization, core and task node health), the Spark History Server and Yarn ResourceManager U I. Fix: resize or add task nodes, managed scaling, tune executors and memory, replace unhealthy nodes, use Spot with fallback for task nodes.

2.title: Performance issues in general
2.text: Performance issues in general. Pipeline slower than usual. Check: Input volume or file count changed, skew, throttling. Fix: Scale out, repartition, compact files, raise capacity. Stream lag. Check: Iterator age, consumer errors, shard limits. Fix: More shards, enhanced fan-out, parallelization factor. Lambda slow or failing. Check: Duration, errors, throttles, memory. Fix: More memory, reserved concurrency, batch size. Redshift queries slow. Check: Queue wait, table design, W L M (workload management). Fix: Sort and distribution keys, concurrency scaling, materialized views. Exam tip: "After a source change, a Glue job is much slower" to check job metrics and the Spark U I for skew or many small files, then fix partitioning and file layout.

2.title: AWS CloudTrail
2.text: A W S CloudTrail. CloudTrail records A P I calls and account activity: who (identity), what (action, resource), when, from where (I P, console, S D K), and result. Event types: management events (control plane: create, delete, change), data events (data plane: S three object reads and writes, Lambda invokes, DynamoDB item access; off by default, extra cost), Insights events (unusual A P I activity). Event history: the console keeps the last ninety days of management events at no charge; for longer retention and all event types create a trail that delivers to S three (and optionally CloudWatch Logs).

2.title: AWS CloudTrail, continued
2.text: A W S CloudTrail, continued. Use it for: who deleted the table, security investigations, compliance, detecting unusual changes; query with Athena or CloudTrail Lake (Module seventeen). Integrity: log file validation shows files were not altered. Exam tip: "Find who dropped a Glue table or changed a bucket policy" to CloudTrail. "CloudWatch shows what the code did; CloudTrail shows who called the A P I.".

2.title: Extracting Logs for Audits
2.text: Extracting Logs for Audits. Plan before you need it: turn on the right logs (CloudTrail trails with data events for sensitive buckets, S three server access logs, V P C flow logs, Glue and Lambda logs, database audit logs for Redshift and R D S (Relational Database Service)) and set retention to match policy. Centralize: deliver logs to one S three bucket (often in a separate log-archive account) with encryption, restricted access and lifecycle rules. Extract: CloudWatch Logs export to S three, subscription filters to Firehose to S three, CloudTrail trail to S three, Athena queries that write results for the auditor, Logs Insights query exports.

2.title: Extracting Logs for Audits, continued
2.text: Extracting Logs for Audits, continued. Preserve evidence: S three Object Lock, versioning, CloudTrail log file validation, restricted delete. Give auditors read-only access to the logs, not to the systems.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Three signals: Metrics (CloudWatch) equals health; logs (CloudWatch Logs) equals what happened; CloudTrail equals who did what. Alarms: O K or alarm or insufficient data; thresholds and periods; composite, anomaly detection; actions: S N S, Lambda, Auto Scaling. Events: EventBridge on Glue or E M R or crawler state changes to S N S or Lambda. Pipeline alarms: Job failed or slow, iterator age, Lambda errors or throttles, D L Q depth, data freshness, zero rows. CloudWatch Logs: Log groups or streams, retention (default never expire), metric filters, subscription filters (Kinesis, Firehose, Lambda), export to S three, Logs Insights (fields filter stats sort). Log analysis: Insights (quick), Athena (S Q L on S three, partition), OpenSearch (search, dashboards), E M R or Spark (huge volumes). Glue or E M R troubleshooting: Glue: metrics, continuous logging, Spark U I, job run insights.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Kestrel Freight wants the on-call team notified whenever an A W S Glue job fails. What is the simplest automated solution? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Glue publishes job state-change events to EventBridge, and a rule can send failures to S N S to notify the team.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Select two. Which two tools are best for querying years of application and CloudTrail logs stored in S three and for near-real-time log search and dashboards respectively? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Athena queries logs in S three cheaply with S Q L, and OpenSearch provides real-time search and dashboards.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. An engineer needs to know who deleted an A W S Glue table last week. Which service provides this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. CloudTrail records A P I calls with the caller identity, the action and the time.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. An E M R cluster is terminated at the end of each job, and the team still needs the step and container logs for troubleshooting. What should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. E M R archives logs to the S three location in the log U R I, so they remain after the cluster terminates.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Select two. An auditor needs evidence of access to a sensitive S three bucket for the past two years. Which two preparations support this? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and D. Data events record object-level access, and a trail with retained logs provides long-term evidence. Event history is limited to ninety days of management events.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: A. Question two: B and D. Question three: A. Question four: C. Question five: C and D. In the next module, we continue the course.
